arms.hypothesis: if GDN run-to-run nondeterminism were an ordering race, a completion barrier would fix it far cheaper than serializing the recurrence
arms.verdict: The completion barrier does not repair the failure. It costs about 1 tok/s (97.211 vs 98.222), while the divergent prompts and token positions are byte-identical to the no-barrier run -- same 8 reported prompt/token pairs. This rules out a missing end-of-op completion dependency as the explanation; it does not by itself identify GDN reduction order or separate GDN from the simultaneously disabled global batch-invariant policies.
no gain (91.371 vs 91.926). The MTP draft head was not padding one-row forwards to four; hypothesis wrong.

optimization_ladder_20260818.conclusion: Validated best under a fresh-compile gate remains 91.926 tok/s at 25/25 self-determinism. The 97-98 tok/s arms do not reproduce across FRESH compile caches. The other machine correctly noted that the fast arm disabled serial-exact GDN and global batch invariance together, so the 6.3 tok/s and the divergence were not causally separated between those two flags -- that attribution is still open. However the divergence itself is now explained: rerunning the fast arm against the FIRST arm's compile cache reproduced it exactly, 25/25 over 12413 tokens. The nondeterminism is in compilation, not runtime. See root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.

root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.finding: The run-to-run nondeterminism that has gated this and the Qwen3.6 lane is in torch.compile/Inductor COMPILATION, not at runtime. Given a fixed compiled artifact the runtime is perfectly deterministic.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.corroboration: The divergent prompts and token positions were byte-identical between the completion-barrier and no-barrier experiments. Random runtime noise would not repeat positions across configs; two different-but-internally-deterministic compilations would, and do.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.why_serial_exact_looked_necessary: serial-exact GDN forces that op to an EAGER graph break, so it is never compiled and never autotuned. It was not buying arithmetic determinism -- it was avoiding the compiler.
root_cause_compilation_nondeterminism.methodological_consequence: The compiled cache is part of the run identity, exactly like the .so binaries the harness already pins by hash. A deployed service compiles once and serves that artifact; reproducibility across restarts with a pinned cache is the operationally meaningful property. This tightens the identity requirement rather than relaxing the gate.

root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.bug: uninitialized read in the persistent GDN spec-decode scratch at 5 verifier rows (MTP4)
evidence: with scratch ON, MTP4 was 24/25 across all three pairs, always failing on holdout--long-rollover-repository-audit

root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.interpretation: the scratch is cached across calls and a region is read before being written at 5 rows, so results depend on whatever the allocator left there. MTP3 at 4 rows writes the whole region, which is why it was clean.
root_cause_persistent_gdn_scratch.WARNING_FOR_SERIAL_EXACT_WORK: gdn_attn_interface.cpp requires VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH=1 whenever serial-exact is enabled. Any MTP4-with-serial-exact build will therefore hit this same uninitialized scratch. The scratch must be zero-initialised, or sized/written correctly for k+1 rows, before that path can be trusted.

async_scheduling_test_20260819.motivation: speculative decoding needs the accepted token ids on the host each step (gpu_model_runner.py:1239-1245) before the next step can be built, so the per-step device-to-host round trip is a serialization point. Async scheduling exists to overlap host scheduling with GPU compute and is explicitly supported alongside spec decode in this vLLM (gpu_input_batch.py:60, gpu_model_runner.py:1780).
async_scheduling_test_20260819.finding_about_the_record: the record runs had async scheduling OFF. SchedulerConfig.async_scheduling defaults to None and get_scheduler_cls tests `if self.async_scheduling:`, which is falsy for None, so the plain Scheduler was used despite the docstring implying on-by-default. Passing --async-scheduling logged 'async_scheduling': True.
async_scheduling_test_20260819.verdict: NEUTRAL. 101.737 / 101.723 against the record's 101.922, inside the +/-1 tok/s run-to-run spread we see across arms. Determinism is unaffected at 25/25. The per-step host round trip is therefore not costing measurable time at this step rate, consistent with 32 cores, one request, and ~35 ms steps. Keep the record configuration; async scheduling is neither a gain nor a risk here, and would only matter at higher concurrency or a much shorter step time.

scratch_fix_projection_correction_202608.their_claim: scratch alloc costs 0.926 ms/step; fix alone lands 103-105; stacked with rerank K=2 reaches 106-109
scratch_fix_projection_correction_202608.what_is_right: the microbenchmark itself is sound - correct TP2/MTP5 shapes, 48 GDN layers, 576 allocations per step - and its anti-validation of the naive zeros-per-call variant (2.435 ms/step, 2.6x worse) is a genuinely useful negative that confirms the fix is only correct because the scratch is cached once per shape.
what_is_wrong: the benchmark calls torch.empty from PYTHON; the production path calls torch::empty from C++ inside gdn_attn_interface.cpp
its own CPU control (0.876 of 0.926 ms) shows ~93% of the measured cost is Python dispatch that does not exist in production
the quoted 'C++ lane cost ~0.3-0.9 ms/step' does not follow from that control; removing dispatch leaves ~0.05 ms
the top of the range (+3.0 tok/s) would require saving ~2.9 ms/step, which exceeds the total the benchmark measured

end_to_end_test_already_run.design: MTP4, three arms each, VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH the ONLY difference
end_to_end_test_already_run.interpretation: disabling caching was +0.237 tok/s. If per-call allocation really cost 0.926 ms/step at a 35.3 ms step, caching would have been about 2.7 tok/s FASTER, not marginally slower. The end-to-end data puts the true cost near 0.05 ms/step, matching the microbenchmark's own control once dispatch is removed.

scratch_fix_projection_correction_202608.still_worth_building: yes - it is the correct fix, it removes a genuine uninitialized read that caused the 24/25 MTP4 failure, and it unblocks serial-exact at depths other than 3. Just not as a route to 105 by itself.

SELF_CORRECTION.what_I_overclaimed: I wrote that the end-to-end MTP4 A/B 'puts the true cost near 0.05 ms/step'. It does not. It failed to DETECT a difference, which is not the same as measuring one near zero.
SELF_CORRECTION.why: the arms spread widely - scratch=1 [101.598, 99.849, 100.26], scratch=0 [101.653, 100.497, 99.905] - giving a per-group sd of about 0.74 and a difference standard error near 0.60 tok/s at n=3. That comparison cannot resolve a ~1.5 tok/s effect with confidence; my observed -0.24 is consistent with anything from roughly -1.7 to +1.2.
SELF_CORRECTION.what_survives: the directional criticism was right and the other machine reached the same conclusion independently: the 0.926 ms/step figure is a Python-dispatch-inclusive upper bound, and 105-from-scratch-fix-alone was never supported.
SELF_CORRECTION.authoritative_number: their op-level A/B on the BUILT fix: 42.87 us/call at PERSISTENT_SCRATCH=0 against 34.08 us/call at =1, i.e. 8.8-9.2 us/call over 48 GDN layers = ~0.42 ms/step = about +1.5 tok/s, projecting ~103.4. That is a real-op measurement and supersedes both my estimate and their original projection.
SELF_CORRECTION.still_outstanding: the strict-25 server rerun with PERSISTENT_SCRATCH=1 on this measuring host. Their own caveat is correct: the op-level parity gate passes on the pinned build too, because a fresh process gets predictable allocator memory, so only long-lived serving residue exposes the bug.

ROOT_CAUSE_CORRECTION.what_I_recorded_first: that per-call allocation of the 12 GDN spec-decode scratch buffers inside a captured graph region faulted the device.
ROOT_CAUSE_CORRECTION.why_that_was_wrong: there was no captured graph region. vllm/config/vllm.py:1047-1052 sets compilation_config.mode = CompilationMode.NONE whenever VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, logging 'VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is set, disabling vLLM's torch.compile pipeline. ROOT_CAUSE_CORRECTION.where_it_actually_faulted: vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/mrope.py:386 forward_xpu -> :321 forward_native -> common.py:222 forward_native -> common.py:177 forward_static -> torch.cat((o1, o2), dim=-1). Rotary embedding on the eager path, nothing to do with GDN scratch.
ROOT_CAUSE_CORRECTION.when: 00:18:00, i.e. 25 s AFTER 'Application startup complete' at 00:17:42 - during the first served request, not during startup or capture.

LEVER_VERDICT.verdict: VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH is NOT a route to more graph capture. It REMOVES compilation. The premise behind testing it - extending capture over the GDN region to reclaim the ~14.2 ms/step of dispatch - was inverted.
LEVER_VERDICT.consequence: do not retry this flag for speed. Any real attack on GDN dispatch has to keep the torch.compile pipeline ON and change splitting_ops / capture, not disable the pipeline.

rerank_topk_audit_20260820.audits: the other machine's 'rerank K=2' proposal, which scratch_fix_projection_correction_20260819.consequence called 'load-bearing for 105'
rerank_topk_audit_20260820.VERDICT_ON_CHEATING: NOT CHEATING. It is draft-side only. The proposal changes what the MTP drafter proposes by rescoring the draft head's own local top-K in FP32 against retained FP16 weights; it does not touch the verifier. vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py:1774-1776 still accepts a draft token only on exact equality with the target argmax, so output equivalence to non-speculative greedy decoding is preserved. Changing the proposal distribution is the one thing speculative decoding is always free to do.

BUT_NOT_LOAD_BEARING.inert_as_scripted: the patched code sits inside a branch gated on VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_INT4 (vocab_parallel_embedding.py:319-326, default off at :74-80). run-arm.sh:464-469 exports only VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_INT4_RERANK_TOPK and has NO passthrough for VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_INT4. The scripted Screen 3 would therefore return baseline and read as a clean null - the SAME inert-arm trap as RETRACTION_scratch_flag_never_applied_20260820.
BUT_NOT_LOAD_BEARING.wrong_control: the record runs VALIDATION_LM_HEAD_INT8=1 with scope 'all', so the MTP draft head is INT8, not INT4. Testing the rerank requires first downgrading the draft head INT8 -> INT4, an unmeasured config change carrying its own acceptance cost. The INT8 record is not the correct control.
BUT_NOT_LOAD_BEARING.cross_rank_flaw: the winner is written back as candidate_values[:, :1] + 1.0 - the rank-local INT4 top-1 score plus a constant. Local logits are all-gathered and argmaxed globally (logits_processor.py:160-166), and every rank adds the same +1.0, so the cross-rank comparison is still decided by INT4 scores. The rerank can only repair rank1<->rank2 flips WITHIN the TP rank that already won on INT4 score. Effect is capped; their note treats the cross-rank path as neutral, which it is not.
BUT_NOT_LOAD_BEARING.gain_unsourced: the '+0.1-0.2 tok/step -> +3 to +6 tok/s' figure has no measurement behind it. The candidate's own status line says 'source-only candidate; not built or measured' and their DO-NOT-REPEAT entry says 'no performance, acceptance, determinism, or quality claim exists yet'.
BUT_NOT_LOAD_BEARING.cost_side: torch.topk over 75968 local vocab x5 draft positions per step, in eager Python in the hot path. sampler.py's own note records a wide topk at ~6x a max reduction on XPU - which is exactly why the deterministic-greedy path was rewritten to avoid topk. This is the same Python-dispatch overhead already identified as dominant.

The B70s are compute-only - console is the ASPEED ast - so unbinding does not disturb the display.

MARGIN_INVALIDATES_PUBLISHED_RECORDS_202.severity: CRITICAL. Both published Qwen3.8 LocalMaxxing records were measured with a setting that changes emitted tokens versus true greedy argmax, and the quality gate that certified them was blind to it by construction.
MARGIN_INVALIDATES_PUBLISHED_RECORDS_202.setting: VALIDATION_DETERMINISTIC_GREEDY_MARGIN=0.03125, present in the commandSnippet of both records.
MARGIN_INVALIDATES_PUBLISHED_RECORDS_202.what_it_does: vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py:44-66. gap = top1 - top2; if gap <= margin it emits min(first_index, second_index). There is NO equality condition on the values: for ANY gap in (0, 0.03125], if the argmax token ID is larger than the runner-up's, the RUNNER-UP is emitted. That is a low-token-ID bias over a finite band, not tie-breaking. It also governs the MTP verifier (rejection_sampler.py:649, 1248, 1440), so it applies at every verified position in the published MTP4/MTP5 configs.

DIRECT_MEASUREMENT_I_VERIFIED.method: compared data/bench.json output_sha256s (25 per arm) between arms whose identity.env differ in EXACTLY one substantive field - deterministic_greedy_margin 0 vs 0.03125. I diffed the full identity.env: the only other difference is the request-id prefix, which is a label.
DIRECT_MEASUREMENT_I_VERIFIED.conclusion: turning the margin off changes generated text on 18 of 25 prompts. The control proves the harness is reproducible at 25/25, so the 18 divergences are attributable to the margin alone.

QUALITY_GATE_IS_CIRCULAR.proof: the quality baseline run qwen38-qualitybaseline-clean-mtp3-fast-25-spec-e-20260818 has deterministic_greedy_margin=0.03125 at run/identity.env:189.
QUALITY_GATE_IS_CIRCULAR.consequence: the gate compares a margin-on candidate against a margin-on baseline by sha256 equality. It is structurally incapable of detecting this variable.
QUALITY_GATE_IS_CIRCULAR.power: the quality suite generates only ~45 tokens total. At the measured flip rate it would pass by luck most of the time even against a margin-free baseline. It cannot detect a ~1-in-360-token flip.

not_a_numerical_noise_device.ulp: fp16 ULP is 0.015625 in [16,32) and 0.0078125 in [8,16), so 0.03125 is 2-4 ULP at the real operating point, not 1 ULP. It captures gaps of 0, 1 ULP and 2 ULP; only gap==0 is a genuine tie.
not_a_numerical_noise_device.int8_head_noise: with the INT8 LM head the per-logit quantization error is ~0.079 and the error on a top1-top2 gap is ~0.112 - roughly 2.5x to 3.6x WIDER than the margin. The margin cannot function as a noise bound in either direction.

MARGIN_INVALIDATES_PUBLISHED_RECORDS_202.never_validated: default is 0 (sampler.py:38), so this is an active opt-in. The value is never derived anywhere; the origin commit has an empty body. The Qwen3.8 margin A/B recorded throughput only (+0.3 tok/s) with no determinism, quality or token-diff field.

It changes the two trajectories differently.' That closeout deliberately submitted nothing. The flag was carried into both submissions the next day anyway.

MARGIN_INVALIDATES_PUBLISHED_RECORDS_202.optimization_upside: dropping the margin is free or positive: the lab's own arm measured 92.237 margin-off vs 91.926 margin-on (+0.3 tok/s). It additionally unblocks two decode fast paths that refuse to engage while it is set - VLLM_XPU_LOCAL_ARGMAX_DECODE and VLLM_XPU_SPEC_GREEDY_TOP_IDS (gpu_model_runner.py:8382, 8451, both returning disabled('deterministic greedy margin needs dense logits')). WHAT_THIS_OVERTURNS.claim: 'nondeterminism is a COMPILATION phenomenon, not arithmetic' - based on two runs sharing a compile cache agreeing 25/25 over 12,413 tokens.
WHAT_THIS_OVERTURNS.why_it_was_wrong: that shared-cache experiment ran with the margin ON. The margin collapses any top1/top2 gap in (0, 0.03125] to the lower token ID, which absorbs exactly the small runtime perturbations that would otherwise flip an argmax. Repeating it margin-free on a shared cache gives 21/25.
WHAT_THIS_OVERTURNS.corrected_conclusion: this stack has GENUINE RUNTIME nondeterminism of roughly one argmax flip per ~3000 tokens, independent of compilation. The margin was concealing it, which is why every determinism gate passed.
WHAT_THIS_OVERTURNS.note: compilation nondeterminism may still exist on TOP of this - fresh-cache arms previously agreed only 12/25 margin-ON. Both effects can be real; only the 'runtime is clean' half is refuted.

MARGIN_WAS_MASKING_RUNTIME_NONDETERMINIS.answers_the_original_question: this is the answer to why the ~95 tok/s result could never be made byte-accurate. It is not a harness artifact and not expected behaviour - it is a real nondeterminism in the serving stack, and the deterministic-greedy margin was papering over it rather than fixing it.

batch_invariance_reopened_20260820.why_reopened: the 2026-08-18 GDN/batch-invariance factorial ran every cell with the deterministic greedy margin ON (that note's own line 49: 'Keep the deterministic greedy margin...'). The margin absorbs any top1/top2 gap in (0, 0.03125] - precisely the small reduction-order perturbations batch invariance exists to remove. So the factorial had almost no headroom in which to observe a determinism benefit, and its determinism readings cannot be used to close the question.
batch_invariance_reopened_20260820.new_headroom: margin-free self-determinism is 21/25 with ~4 independent flip events in 12,413 tokens. That is real, measurable headroom for a determinism fix to close.

DEAD_KNOB_NEEDS_A_ONE_LINE_FIX.bug: linear.py:227-237. xpu_batch_invariant is computed as current_platform.is_xpu() AND the env var, but the branch is then guarded by 'if (envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT or xpu_batch_invariant) and current_platform.is_cuda_alike():'. is_cuda_alike() is defined at platforms/interface.py:191-193 as _enum in (CUDA, ROCM), and XPU's _enum is PlatformEnum.XPU (platforms/xpu.py:33). is_xpu() and is_cuda_alike() are mutually exclusive, so the XPU branch is unreachable dead code.
DEAD_KNOB_NEEDS_A_ONE_LINE_FIX.fix: change the guard to '(envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT and current_platform.is_cuda_alike()) or xpu_batch_invariant'
DEAD_KNOB_NEEDS_A_ONE_LINE_FIX.scope_caveat: this is UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply. The model is INT4-quantized, so most GEMMs take the quantized path and would be unaffected; expect limited reach until the quantized paths get an equivalent.
DEAD_KNOB_NEEDS_A_ONE_LINE_FIX.defect_class: this is the THIRD flag found to silently do nothing, after VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_PERSISTENT_SCRATCH and VLLM_XPU_DDTREE_CAPTURE_GDN_CORE. Verify a flag reached AND changed behaviour before trusting any arm that sets it.

That makes it bisectable: a reduced suite of those 4 prompts reproduces the whole phenomenon and would cut determinism-test cost by roughly 6x. Note B-vs-C is the cleanest comparison (both fully warm, no compilation during the run) and still shows 3 divergent prompts, so the effect is not an artifact of compiling during arm A.

rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.verdict: NEGATIVE. Batch-invariant RMSNorm does NOT fix the runtime nondeterminism. Reject it.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.flag_verified_LIVE: yes, and this matters given three other flags were no-ops. identity.env:92 rmsnorm_batch_invariant=1, and the arm's tokens differ from the non-BI arms on 14-16 of 25 prompts, so the op genuinely changed the arithmetic rather than silently doing nothing.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.self_determinism: 21/25 - identical to the no-BI baseline (21/25, 21/25, 22/25). 549 divergent tokens / 12056.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.same_prompts_same_positions: the SAME four prompts diverge, at nearly identical token positions: sql-debugging@35 (was @35), structured-extraction@225 (was @225), long-rollover-repository-audit@469 (was @469), factual-protocol@311 (was @465).
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.cost: D 100.639 / D' 101.372 all-25, median ~101.0 against the no-BI median 101.170. Effectively free - but free and useless.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.shared_cache_proof: arm D compiled 132.82 s; arm D' 5.11 s.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.WHAT_THIS_TELLS_US: the divergence survives a substantial change to RMSNorm arithmetic and reappears at the SAME token positions. So RMSNorm is not the source, and more importantly those positions are where the model sits at a genuine decision boundary - near-tied logits that ANY small run-to-run perturbation will flip. Finding the culprit therefore means finding any ubiquitous source of run-to-run variation, not a prompt-specific bug.
rmsnorm_batch_invariance_NEGATIVE_202608.next_hypothesis: the TP2 allreduce is the leading candidate: oneCCL reduction order can vary run to run and it is ubiquitous across every layer. A TP1 run would be decisive - no allreduce at all. If TP1 self-determinism is 25/25, the collective is the source.

PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.severity: CRITICAL and BLOCKING. The host is serving corrupted model data through the normal read path. All GPU work is stopped.
PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.discovery: the harness model-identity guard rejected a run with 'SHA256 mismatch for model-00002-of-00007.safetensors'. That guard did its job.

the_finding.conclusion: THE DISK IS FINE. The page cache is serving corrupted data. dd iflag=direct returns the correct bytes; ordinary reads return corrupt bytes.
the_finding.persistent: the corruption is sticky, not a one-off. Two ordinary hash passes agreed on the wrong value, and a third ordinary read AFTER a correct direct read still returned the wrong value.
the_finding.not_memory_pressure: 125 GB total, 90 GB free, 120 GB available at the time of measurement.
the_finding.filesystem: /dev/sda2 on /mnt/usb-models, type fuseblk (NTFS-3G via FUSE), rw,relatime,blksize=4096. File mtime is unchanged since 2026-08-15 23:10 and a full sequential read completes without I/O error.

PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.WHY_THIS_MATTERS_BEYOND_THE_GUARD: vLLM loads safetensors weights through ordinary reads/mmap, which go through the same page cache. A process starting now would load CORRUPTED WEIGHTS and would not necessarily fail loudly - it would just compute slightly wrong numbers.
PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.NEW_HYPOTHESIS_FOR_THE_NONDETERMINISM: this is a candidate explanation for the 21/25 margin-free self-determinism. If the page cache intermittently serves corrupt weight bytes, two runs loading the same shards can end up with slightly different weights, which would flip exactly the near-tied argmax positions that were observed to diverge. NOT yet tested - it is a hypothesis, and it competes with the TP2 allreduce hypothesis.

WHICH_RESULTS_ARE_AFFECTED.probably_clean: every arm run today up to and including the fast-paths arm, because each logged 'model revision and all recorded file identities verified' at startup. The margin-free baseline arms, the RMSNorm-BI arms and the fast-paths arm all passed that check.
WHICH_RESULTS_ARE_AFFECTED.suspect: anything after roughly 02:11 local. The first GDN-capture 25-prompt attempt passed model-verify and then hung in API server startup at 02:11 - that hang may well be an early symptom rather than a flake.
WHICH_RESULTS_ARE_AFFECTED.recommendation: re-verify the whole model with direct I/O, and re-run any result that matters, after the cache is cleared.

PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.REMEDY_NEEDS_ROOT: drop the page cache (echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches) or unmount and remount /mnt/usb-models, then re-verify all seven shards with dd iflag=direct. Longer term, NTFS-3G over FUSE is a poor store for multi-GB weights under sustained load; a native filesystem would be materially safer. NOT performed - privileged action, needs Steve's go-ahead.
PAGE_CACHE_CORRUPTION_20260820.status: all GPU experimentation is halted. The harness will reject every run while the cached hash mismatches, which is correct behaviour.
